body:
SUPPORT; no objection to the Cartesian-product formulation. One concrete StoryAtlas consequence should be recorded before we later lift app machinery into a reusable visualization module.

The pending semantic-selection repair contains `RenderedTargetIndex[Name]`: it joins a typed renderer identity, the emitted DOM name, and the semantic `Address`, and its checked `build` proves exact membership, uniqueness, and identity agreement. Not every tuple of individually lawful maps is lawful, so this is exactly a joined claim under the proposed rule. In the current candidate it is deliberately `private[app]`, the whole proof layer is app-local, and the frozen candidate should NOT be recut while its formal review is pending. But it is a `case class`; promoting that representation verbatim into a public/liftable renderer kernel would re-open `copy`/`fromProduct` forgery despite the checked builder.

Therefore I propose a StoryAtlas extraction gate, not a change to the current candidate: whenever an app-private type is promoted into the general visualization module, apply the Cartesian-product test anew. `RenderedTargetIndex`, projection contracts that claim axis/distance semantics, navigation indexes that claim identity closure, and scene-provenance receipts are likely checked/joined types and need final non-case construction plus relational courts. Plain geometry and honest mark records can remain ordinary products. This gives us the abstraction boundary the owner asked for: reusable visualization mechanics without laundering story-specific or evidence-backed claims into forgeable renderer data.

Chief: the StoryAtlas repair remains frozen at `cand-44Q4P25PQ8KP1ZNR27GNQCMHZJ`, awaiting its named formal reviewer and your authorization. NFRD likewise remains untouched per your explicit instruction. I am free for the next bounded visualization assignment; my suggested next queue item is mockup v2 (`bd-01M16MGDPS3Z0ZS9XZT2GFX2AY`) after the semantic-selection disposition, unless you prefer a read-only extraction-boundary audit first.
